sentences.text:
Kanai Paria & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal on 18 December,
2017
Author: Debi Prosad Dey
Bench: Debi Prosad Dey

In The High Court At Calcutta Sl.14 (Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction) Ct-35
Appellate Side (Ad) C.R.R. No.2020 of 2016 In the matter of: Kanai Paria & Anr.
vs. The State of West Bengal Mr. Abhijit Kumar ADhya.

Adv.
...for the petitioners.
Ms. Anusua Sinha.

Adv.
...
for the State.

Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order No.15 dated June 8, 2016, this criminal revisional application has been filed on the ground that the State amendment of Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code has become infractuous in view of the judgment delivered by this Court reported in (2007) 2 Cr LR (Cal) 737 (M/s. Bhaskar Tea & Industries Ltd. -vs- The State.

Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners contends that the report of the expert does not reveal that obnoxious materials were used in the alleged adulteration of the mustard oil and accordingly, the offence ought to be tried by learned Magistrate in stead of by learned Sessions Judge.
In support of his contention, learned Advocate for the petitioners has referred to the aforesaid decision as well as a decision reported in AIR 1983 SC 150.

Ms. Anusua Sinha, learned Advocate appearing for the State, submits that the factual aspect of the case under reference cannot be looked into in a revisional application and that Section 272 along with the State amendment has not yet been declared unconstitutional by the Hon'ble Apex Court.

Ms. Sinha further submits that the case ought to be tried by learned Sessions Judge and there is absolutely no illegality in the order passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court-III, Howrah.

sentences.text: The order dated 8th June, 2016 reveals that the prayer of the defence to the effect that the matter should be disposed of by learned Magistrate has been rejected and that the learned Trial Court did not take into consideration the decision referred to hereinabove holding, inter alia, that Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code has not yet been declared unconstitutional by the concerned Court.

The decision reported in AIR 1983 SC 150 reveals that the Hon'ble Apex Court has considered lesser punishment of the appellant in view of Section 16(1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954.
The decision referred to hereinabove of our High Court also does not repeal Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code.

In that view of this case, the case is under reference ought to be tried by learned Sessions Judge/Additional Sessions Judge, I do not find any illegality in the order No.15 dated June 8, 2016 passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, Howrah and accordingly, the criminal revisional application being C.R.R. No.2020 of 2016 stands dismissed.
Let a copy of this order be forwarded to the learned Court below for information and necessary action.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, shall be given to the parties as expeditiously as possible on compliance of all necessary formalities.
(Debi Prosad Dey, J.)
